get.summary: Finish signing in with the identity provider
get.description: Where the identity provider sends the browser back: a GET that needs no session and no CSRF header, the flow cookie and `state` being what ties it to the start. Limited to 60 callbacks per client address in 15 minutes, counted apart from password sign-in failures (a callback can never lock anyone out of password sign-in); without a provider nothing is counted and the answer is `config`. Over the limit the browser is sent to `/sign-in?sso_error=rate_limited`.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code the identity provider made.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` of the attempt.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: The error code when the identity provider refused.

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: Ignored.

302.description: Signed in: the session cookie is set and the browser is sent to the path given at the start (`/` when it was not a console path). Not signed in: the browser is sent to `/sign-in?sso_error=<code>` with code `state`, `expired`, `idp`, `token`, `not_allowed`, `disabled`, `rate_limited` or `config`. The flow cookie is cleared either way.

Location.description: The console path, or the sign-in page with the reason.

Set-Cookie.description: The cleared flow cookie, and the session cookie when signed in.

get.summary: Start signing in with the identity provider
get.description: A browser navigation, not a call for a script: a GET that needs no session and no CSRF header. Limited to 60 starts per client address in 15 minutes, counted apart from sign-in failures; over the limit the browser is sent to `/sign-in?sso_error=rate_limited` and a flow cookie already set is left alone.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Where to send the browser after sign-in: a path inside the console that starts with a single `/`. Anything else means `/`.

302.description: The browser is sent to the identity provider. The flow cookie `uf_oidc` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/auth/oidc, 10 minutes) is set. Without a provider that can be reached, to `/sign-in?sso_error=config`; over the start limit, to `/sign-in?sso_error=rate_limited` (no cookie is set).

404.description: `oidc_disabled`: single sign-on is not turned on.

get.summary:
Downloads a consistent copy of the database: a SQLite file with every
table, taken of one moment while the gateway goes on. It holds
everything the database holds (users with their password hashes,
sessions, logs, provider credentials as they are stored) except the
master key, which is not in it: the credentials are unreadable without
that key, and so the copy is of little use without it. Admin only; the
download is audited. On PostgreSQL there is no file to give: 409
`backup_unsupported`, with the advice to use `pg_dump`.

200.description: The database as a SQLite file.

401.description: No valid session or access token.

403.description: The caller is not allowed to do this.

409.description: The database is PostgreSQL, which is backed up with pg_dump (code backup_unsupported).

Filters only narrow what the caller may see.
get.description:
What a caller sees depends on who they are. An admin sees every row. A
team lead sees the rows of the teams they lead, the rows of the users who
are members of those teams, and their own. Anyone else sees their own
rows. A lead's scope uses the CURRENT membership: a row linked to a team
only by its user leaves the lead's view when that user leaves the team.
Rows of keys without an owner are visible to admins only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows to return, 1 to 200. 50 when left out.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The id of the last row of the page before.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only calls at or after this time: RFC 3339, or a date `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC, from its start).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only calls at or before this time: RFC 3339, or a date `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC, to its end).

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: Only calls made with this key.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Only calls of this user.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Only calls of this team.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Only calls answered by, or asking for, this model name.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only calls answered with this HTTP status, 100 to 599.

parameters.name: errors
parameters.description: `true`: only calls answered with a status of 400 or more. Combines with the other filters.

parameters.name: guardrail
parameters.description: Only calls whose worst guardrail action was this: `blocked`, `redacted` or `flagged` (a block is worse than a redaction, a redaction worse than a flag). Combines with the other filters.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only calls with this tag, written `name:value` (the name ends at the first colon). Repeat it to require several tags: all must match.

200.description: The calls the caller may see, newest first.

get.summary: Sums of the calls in a range of days, by day, model, key, user or team.
get.description:
What a caller sees depends on who they are, as in the log list. An admin
sees every call. A team lead sees the calls of the teams they lead, the
calls of the users who are members of those teams, and their own. Anyone
else sees their own calls, so grouping by user or team shows only
themselves and the teams on their own calls. A lead's scope uses the
CURRENT membership: a call linked to a team only by its user leaves the
lead's totals when that user leaves the team. Calls of keys without an
owner count for admins only. Days are UTC. The range is at most 366 days;
it defaults to the last 30 days.

The CSRF token of the session. `null` for a caller with an access
token.

MemberDetail.description: A member of a team, with what names them.

input_price_micros.description: Per million tokens, in millionths of a dollar. `null`: not known.

What a million input tokens cost, in millionths of a dollar. `null`
is unknown: calls of the model are logged with cost 0, unpriced.

name.description: The provider's own id for the model.

output_price_micros.description: What a million output tokens cost, in millionths of a dollar.

issuer.description: The issuer to test. Left out or empty: the saved one.

error.description: What is wrong, when `ok` is false. It never repeats a URL.

issuer.description: The issuer the provider named, when its discovery document was read.

jwks_keys.description: How many keys the provider publishes to verify ID tokens.

ok.description: Whether the discovery document and the key set could be used.

OidcUpdateRequest.description:
Every setting. A field left out takes its default, except
`client_secret`: left out, the stored secret is kept.

allowed_domains.description: At most 100 domains; stored in lower case.

auto_create.description: Needs at least one allowed domain. Default false.

client_id.description: At most 512 bytes. May be empty while single sign-on is off.

client_secret.description:
Write only: replaces the stored secret. Left out: the stored secret
stays. At most 4096 bytes.

enabled.description: Needs `UF_PUBLIC_URL`, an issuer, a client id and a client secret.

issuer.description:
An `https` URL (`http` only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1]),
without credentials, query or fragment. May be empty while single
sign-on is off.

admin_group.description:
Members of this group become admins on sign-in; empty: roles are
never changed by sign-in.

auto_create.description:
Whether a person from an allowed domain gets a Member account on
first sign-in.

client_secret_set.description:
Whether a client secret is stored. The secret itself is never
returned.

client_secret_unreadable.description:
True when a secret is stored but cannot be decrypted (the master key
changed). Single sign-on stays off until a new secret is saved.

enabled.description: Whether the sign-in button is offered.

groups_claim.description: The ID token claim that lists the user's groups.

issuer.description: The issuer URL of the identity provider; empty until set.

label.description: The name on the button: "Sign in with <label>".

link_by_email.description:
Whether a person who signs in is matched to an existing user by a
verified email address.

public_url_set.description:
Whether the gateway was started with `UF_PUBLIC_URL`. Single
sign-on cannot be turned on without it.

redirect_uri.description:
The address to register at the identity provider; null without a
public URL.

scopes.description: Scopes asked for besides `openid email profile`, space separated.

OutcomeView.description: What a check found. Holds counts and ids only, never matched text.

oneOf.description:
The first guardrail that blocks the text; `id` is 0 for rules sent
with the request.

redactions.description: Replacements made, by PII type (`EMAIL`) or by rule id.

PlaygroundChatAnswer.description: The answer of `/v1/chat/completions`, in the OpenAI shape.

PlaygroundChatRequest.description:
A chat request, as `/v1/chat/completions` takes it. The body is read by
the same parser as that call's, so any field it accepts is accepted here.

model.description: A model as `provider/name`, or a route name.

tool_choice.description: `auto`, `none`, `required` or a named function, as in `/v1/chat/completions`. Without `tools`, `required` and a named function are refused with 400.

tools.description: Functions the model may call, as in `/v1/chat/completions`.

PlaygroundErrorBody.description:
An error of this call: the CSRF and sign-in errors have the `/api` shape
(`code`, `message`); the pipeline's own have the OpenAI shape (`message`,
`type`, and sometimes `code`).

code.description: `null` in the OpenAI shape, except for a spent budget.

type.description: Only in the OpenAI shape, such as `permission_error`.

content.description: Text, or a list of parts (`text` and `image_url`) as in `/v1/chat/completions`. Null is allowed on an assistant message that has `tool_calls`. Images are `data:` URLs or, except for Gemini, `http(s)` URLs, and count toward the request body limit (10 MiB).

tool_call_id.description: On a `tool` message: the id of the call it answers.

tool_calls.description: The calls of an assistant message, as in `/v1/chat/completions`.

weight.description: Share of the traffic among the primaries, 1 to 1000.

model_id.description: Zero for a caller who is not an admin.

weight.description: Zero for a caller who is not an admin.

ProviderView.description:
A provider as `/api` shows it: whether it has a credential, never the
credential.

base_url.description: Where the provider is called. Admins only: `null` for anybody else.

invite_link.description:
The link that lets the user set a password. It is shown once, in
this answer, and cannot be read again.

Role.description: A user's role in the organization.

secret.description:
The new signing secret. It is shown once, in this answer, and cannot
be read again.

fallbacks.description: `provider/model`, in the order they are tried.

guardrails.description:
Names of guardrails, in the order they apply. Left out of the file
for a route that has none; a file that leaves it out does not change
what is attached (`[]` takes them all off).

cache_enabled.description:
Keep the answers of calls to this route and give them again to the
same call, without a provider. Streams and calls with a temperature
above 0.5 are never kept. Not sent: off.

cache_scope.description:
Whom a kept answer is given to: `team` (the team of the key; a key
with no team uses `user`, then `key`), `key` or `user`. Never across
teams. Not sent: `team`.

cache_ttl_s.description: How long an answer is kept, 1 to 86 400 seconds. Not sent: 300.

everyone.description:
Every user may use the route. It cannot be combined with teams.
Without it and without teams only admins may use the route.

fallbacks.description: Model ids, tried in this order when the primaries fail.

guardrail_ids.description:
The guardrails applied to calls of this route, in this order, after
the gateway-wide ones. At most 20. Left out, the route keeps the ones
it has; `[]` takes them all off.

name.description:
1 to 64 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`, starting with a
letter or digit. No `/`, so a route never reads as `provider/model`.

primaries.description: At least one. A model appears at most once in the route.

team_ids.description: Teams that may use the route.

total_timeout_ms.description: 1 000 to 3 600 000, not below the first token timeout.

RouteView.description:
A route. For a caller who is not an admin, `model_id`, `weight`, every
setting, `everyone` and `team_ids` are hidden: they read as 0, false or
empty whatever they are. Only the names and flags of the targets are real.

broken.description: No target of the route is enabled, so it cannot serve a request.

cache_enabled.description: The route keeps answers. Hidden (false) for a non-admin.

cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds an answer is kept. Hidden (0) for a non-admin.

everyone.description: Every user may use the route. Hidden (false) for a non-admin.

guardrails.description:
The guardrails applied to calls of this route, in order. Hidden
(empty) for a non-admin.

directions.description: The directions the rule applies to.

id.description: Stable within a guardrail; the label of keyword/regex redaction counts.

firing.description: What it is firing for now.

params.description: The parameters with every default written out.

amount_micros.description: The amount in millionths of a dollar: 1 to 1 000 000 000 000 000.

scope_id.description: The id of the team, user or key. Not sent for the gateway.
The id of the team, user or key. Not sent for the gateway.

log_retention_days.description: 1 to 3650. Not in the file: not changed.

session_hours.description: 1 to 720. Not in the file: not changed.

database.description:
The database the gateway runs on. Read only: `UF_DATABASE_URL` set
means `postgres`. A PostgreSQL database is not backed up from here
(use `pg_dump`).

log_retention_days.description: How many days request logs are kept before they are deleted.

session_hours.description:
How many hours a session lives, from sign-in. Sessions that exist
keep the lifetime they were made with.

trusted_proxies.description:
The networks (CIDR) whose forwarding headers are believed, as the
gateway was started. Read only: it is a flag of `ultrafast serve`.

setup_code.description:
The one-time code the gateway printed to its log when it started
without users. Required; left out or wrong, the answer is 403.

SideLog.description: The checks of one direction (the input of a call, or its output).

action.description: The worst thing that happened in this direction.

oneOf.description: The guardrail that blocked, when one did.

checked_with.description: The guardrails this direction was checked with.

redactions.description: Replacements made, by PII type or rule id.

label.description: The name for the sign-in button.

oneOf.description: The single sign-on provider, when it is on; `null` otherwise.

password.description: Always true: passwords are never turned off.

added.description: The names that were new, now in the catalog and disabled.

existing.description: How many names the provider listed that were already there.

TargetHealth.description: The health of one target, as `GET /api/routing/health` shows it.

failures.description: Retryable failures. A request the provider rejected is not one.

last_failure_at.description: When the last of those happened (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`).

last_status.description:
What the provider answered to the last of them; none when it did not
answer.

TargetState.description: What the breaker of a target allows now.

TeamRole.description: A user's role inside one team.

TeamSummary.description: A team with the number of its members.

TestResult.description: What a test delivery came to.

error.description: Why it failed. Never holds the URL.

status.description: The HTTP status the receiver answered with, if it answered.

TokenStatus.description: Whether a token can still be used, as of the moment of the answer.

TokenView.description: A token as `/api` shows it. It has no field for the token or its hash.

status.description: Worked out when the answer is made.

UpdateKeyRequest.description: What to change on a key. Admins only; send at least one field.

guardrail_ids.description:
Replaces the guardrails of the key; `[]` takes them all off. Left
out, they stay.

tags.description:
Replaces all the tags of the key; `{}` removes them. The same limits
as when the key is created. Left out, the tags stay.

enabled.description: Left out, the model stays as it is.

input_price_micros.description:
Millionths of a dollar per million input tokens, 0 or more. Left
out, the price stays; `null` makes it unknown.

api_key.description: Absent leaves the key, `null` removes it, a string replaces it.

kind.description: Only the kind the rule has; it cannot change.

params.description: Replaces the parameters. What the rule is firing for is forgotten.

session_hours.description: 1 to 720. Applies to sessions made from now on.

from.description: First day of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC.

to.description: Last day of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC.

UsageRow.description: Sums over one group of calls.

cancelled.description:
Calls the caller abandoned before they were answered (status 499): not
errors of the gateway or of a provider.

errors.description: Calls answered with a status of 400 or more, except 499.

group.description:
The day (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the model name, or the id of the key, user or
team. Empty for calls that have no key, user or team. `total` in the
total row.

input_tokens.description:
Includes the tokens of cached answers (`cached` rows of the logs),
which cost nothing.

label.description:
What to show: the day, the model name, the key or team name, the
user's email, `(none)` for calls without a key, user or team,
`(deleted)` when that object is gone, `Total` in the total row.

unpriced_requests.description:
Calls that reported token usage but could not be priced, so their
cost is missing from `cost_micros`.

UserStatus.description: The state of a user account.

UserTeamView.description: A team of a user, with their role in it.

UserView.description: A user as `/api` shows it. It has no field for the password hash.

auth_provider.description:
How the user signs in: with a `password`, or through the single
sign-on provider (`oidc`) they are linked to. Read only.

has_password.description:
Whether the user has a password. A user made by single sign-on has
none and can sign in only while single sign-on works. Read only.

teams.description: The user's teams, ordered by name.

session.name: uf_session
session.description: The session cookie set by signing in.

token.description: An access token, which starts with `uf-at-`.
